solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Experts taking steps when power is lost

indicators.note: something that is lost has gone missing, so a letter drops out of the word for steps

parts.note: steps or strides are paces
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: Specialists only manage to keep walking when the electricity fails.
explanation.definitionFit: Aces are people who are outstanding at something, synonyms for experts.

clue.text: Insurance — attack sum added to bill

parts.note: insurance is cover against loss
to charge is to attack, as cavalry do

explanation.surface: An insurer's assault on the bill reads like a stealthy surcharge.
explanation.definitionFit: A restaurant or club fee tacked on to the bill for service or entry is a synonym for the definition.

clue.text: Place that's holy almost has ruler drawing back

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the holy place is left off

parts.note: a shrine is a holy place
a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: A sanctuary is retreating because a monarch is pulling it back.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrinking from something is recoiling or pulling away from it, a synonym of drawing back.

clue.text: Sadder group collecting one prestigious award

indicators.note: collecting means gathering in, so the group takes the letter for one inside it

parts.note: blue means sad, so sadder is bluer
a band is a group of musicians
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A rather gloomy band picks up a top prize.
explanation.definitionFit: The Blue Riband is a famous honour, originally for the fastest Atlantic liner crossing, so an emblem of the top achievement.

clue.text: Little donkey fed with Italian or Mexican food

indicators.note: being fed with something means having it put inside, so the donkey takes the Italian into its middle

parts.note: a burro is a small donkey
IT is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and it

explanation.surface: A small donkey is given either Italian or Mexican fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A burrito is a Mexican dish of a tortilla wrapped round a filling.

clue.text: Somehow doing my nut, complainer being scathing

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters of my nut and complainer arrive in some unspecified new order

explanation.surface: A grumbler is driving me mad with harsh remarks.
explanation.definitionFit: Scathing criticism is harshly critical, the opposite of flattering, which is what the answer means.

clue.text: Survive journey away from home

parts.note: a ride is a journey
someone not at home is out

explanation.surface: A trip taken while away seems a matter of getting through it.
explanation.definitionFit: To ride out a storm or crisis is to come through it safely, so to survive it.

clue.text: Proof of who you are needed in Lincoln to stay

indicators.note: something needed in a place has to go inside it, so the identity papers go within Lincoln

parts.note: Abe is the nickname of US President Abraham Lincoln
ID is identification

explanation.surface: You must show identification if you want to stay in the city of Lincoln.
explanation.definitionFit: To abide somewhere is an old-fashioned way of saying to remain or dwell there.

clue.text: Approximately five hundred turn up making public protests

indicators.note: in a down clue, turn up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: some means approximately, as in some fifty people
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

explanation.surface: Around five hundred people show up to make their protest heard.
explanation.definitionFit: Demos is the short informal word for demonstrations, which are public protests.

clue.text: Hesitation shown by papa in awful divorce requiring much outlay

indicators.note: in places the hesitation and papa inside the rearranged letters
awful suggests the word divorce is messed up into a new order

parts.note: er is a sound of hesitation
P is papa in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A messy divorce, with a father dithering, ends up costing a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' signals the anagram of divorce, and 'in' places the hesitation plus papa within those rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overpriced costs too much, so buying it calls for a large outlay of money.

clue.text: Old country fellow travelling round India

indicators.note: travelling round means going around, so the fellow's name encloses the letter for India

parts.note: Sam is a typical man's name, standing for any fellow
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A man is touring around India.
explanation.definitionFit: Siam was the former name of Thailand, so it is an old country name.

clue.text: Country character of yesteryear in small piece (not leader in Times)

indicators.note: in places the old character inside the shortened small piece
not means without, so a letter is taken away from the small piece

parts.note: a bit is a small piece

indicators.note: the leader in a word is its first letter

parts.note: a rune is a letter of an ancient alphabet

explanation.surface: A historical figure appears briefly in a newspaper article, but not on the front page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' takes away the 'leader in Times' from the small piece; 'in' then sets the ancient character inside what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunei is a small sultanate on the island of Borneo.

clue.text: Desolate areas sheltering revolutionary types disinclined to act

indicators.note: sheltering means protecting within, so the moorland holds the revolutionary inside

parts.note: moors are bleak upland areas
Che Guevara is the classic crossword revolutionary

explanation.surface: Bleak moorland hides rebels who can't be bothered to do anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Moochers are idlers who loaf about, so people reluctant to do anything.

clue.text: Share of top people who may discount religious claims?

parts.note: a ration is a fixed share
the A-list is the top tier of celebrities

explanation.surface: Some of the elite are sceptics who dismiss religion.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationalist bases belief on reason rather than faith, so is likely to reject religious claims.

clue.text: What's said to restrict someone in the Far East

indicators.note: what's said points to the sound of a word rather than its spelling

parts.note: to tie is to restrict or bind

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about how to confine a person in East Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: A Thai is a person from Thailand, a country in South East Asia, loosely the Far East.

clue.text: Get rid of religious type keeping unorthodox rite

indicators.note: keeping means holding within, so the religious person contains the rearranged rite

parts.note: an oblate is a lay person dedicated to religious life

indicators.note: unorthodox means not following the usual pattern, so the letters of rite are rearranged

explanation.surface: Expel a devotee who keeps to a heretical ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unorthodox' signals an anagram of rite, and 'keeping' places those letters inside the religious type, a lay person dedicated to a monastery.
explanation.definitionFit: To obliterate is to wipe out or destroy completely, a strong synonym of removing.

clue.text: Address about to be given border with neighbour? Engineers brought in

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: brought in means placed inside, so the engineers go within the border

parts.note: a fence marks the border with next door's garden
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Sounds like a property dispute: an address about the fence with next door, with engineers called in.
explanation.definitionFit: To make reference to something is to mention or address it.

clue.text: Person at concert receiving good artist, one giving coded messages?

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the concert-goer holds the good artist inside

parts.note: a prommer attends the Proms, the BBC's summer series of London concerts
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A concert-goer is handed a fine painter, who passes secret notes.
explanation.definitionFit: A programmer writes code, the instructions given to a computer, playfully seen as coded messages.

clue.text: Endlessly praise a learner, a cadet who really made it?

definitions.text: a cadet who really made it?

indicators.note: endlessly means without its end, so the last letter of the praise word goes

parts.note: to admire is to praise or esteem
L is the learner sign on British learner drivers' cars

explanation.surface: Heap praise on a trainee, a cadet who has risen to the very top.
explanation.definitionFit: A naval cadet who rises to the highest rank becomes a fleet commander, so has truly succeeded.

clue.text: Chicken maybe turning yellow with boss losing head

indicators.note: turning means the heraldic word for yellow is read backwards

parts.note: or is gold or yellow in heraldry

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter of the boss word is dropped

parts.note: a master is a boss

explanation.surface: A chicken goes yellow as its owner is beheaded.
explanation.definitionFit: A roaster is a bird fit for roasting, and a chicken is the usual example.

clue.text: Measure brought by Labour leader of yesteryear

definitions.meaning: a unit of length, twelve inches
Michael ... led the British Labour Party from 1980 to 1983

explanation.surface: A policy introduced by a former Labour chief.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a unit of length and the surname of Michael Foot, Labour leader in the early 1980s.

clue.text: Spooner's jolly enthusiast who may operate in the underworld?

definitions.text: who may operate in the underworld?

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the starting sounds of words, so the first letters of the two words trade places

parts.note: merry means jolly
a fan is an enthusiast

explanation.surface: A cheerful supporter turns out to be a gangster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'operate in the underworld' suggests crime; it means Charon, who rowed souls across the Styx to Hades in Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Charon, the boatman of Hades, carries the dead across the river into the realm below.

clue.text: One desperately wanting knowledge very quick to engage university

indicators.note: to engage means to take on or hold, so the quick word holds the university letter

parts.note: fast means very quick

explanation.surface: A desperate student rushes to enrol at university.
explanation.definitionFit: In legend the scholar sold his soul to the Devil in exchange for knowledge and power.

clue.text: Charity event with endless chat and music

parts.note: a rag is a student charity event in British universities

indicators.note: endless means losing the final letter of the chat word

parts.note: gab is chat

explanation.surface: A fundraiser offers non-stop talk and some music.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragga is a style of Jamaican dance music derived from reggae and dancehall.

clue.text: Freely moving about, using a minor highway

parts.note: ... is a secondary road in Britain, below an A road

explanation.surface: Getting around easily by taking a side road.
explanation.definitionFit: An old sense of the word is out and about, at large and moving freely.

clue.text: Impulse our gentlemen must restrain

indicators.note: to restrain is to hold in, so the words our gentlemen hold the answer within them

explanation.surface: Our men have to keep their desires in check.
explanation.definitionFit: An urge is a strong impulse or desire.

clue.text: Sport later modified somewhere in Ireland

indicators.note: modified means changed, so the letters of later are rearranged

parts.note: Ennis is the county town of Clare in Ireland

explanation.surface: A game later changed somewhere in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Real tennis is the ancient indoor racket game from which lawn tennis developed.

clue.text: Drink with politician, Left philosopher who works willingly with others?

parts.note: tea is a drink
MP is a Member of Parliament
A. J. Ayer was a British philosopher

explanation.surface: Having a cuppa with an MP and a left-wing thinker suggests cooperation.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone cooperative who puts the group's interest first is called this, from team sports.

clue.text: Triumphs, putting out fine food

indicators.note: putting out means removing, so the letter for fine is taken out

parts.note: feats are triumphs or achievements
F is short for fine on pencil grades

explanation.surface: Victories, laying on good grub.
explanation.definitionFit: Eats is informal for food.
